values.note: Showers in Bear Paw and Pine Ridge from the fishing opener through the first Sunday in October; flush toilets seasonal, vault toilets year-round. The seasonal dump station is in Bear Paw; an off-season one is on the winter access road into Pine Ridge.

values.note: Pine Ridge's Oak & Spruce loops (electric) are in season through the winter; Maple and Pine & Poplar close after November 15 and Bear Paw was already closed for the season on November 12.

note: Two drive-in campgrounds: Pine Ridge (four wooded loops) and Bear Paw near the east arm of Lake Itasca, set back about 150 ft behind trees and marsh; Bear Paw also has 11 cart-in sites. Backpack sites and a group camp elsewhere in the park. Pinned to Pine Ridge. --Claude
summary: DNR + ReserveMN: 223 drive-in sites (160 electric, 50 amp), 60-ft limit (pads 25-90 ft, all 23 ft+), showers/flush/vault/dump, Pine Ridge Oak & Spruce open all winter. Fees as stored ($25/$35 June 2027). PIN WRONG: stored point is a building parking lot ~4.7 km SE - move to Pine Ridge. Not waterfront kept.
flags: PIN MOVE (~4.7 km): stored 47.19520,-95.16600 is a parking lot beside large buildings near the park entrance road (apparently the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center area), not a campground, although the note says 'Pinned to Pine Ridge'. Pine Ridge loops (ReserveMN unit coordinates, Oak & Spruce centroid 47.23306,-95.19072, Maple 47.23442,-95.19073, Pine & Poplar 47.23615,-95.19075; confirmed as campsite loops on Esri imagery): move to 47.23400,-95.19070. Bear Paw's units centre 47.21862,-95.18990 if the reviewer prefers it.
Phone: none stored. DNR contact '218-699-7251' (park office). apply.py does not write phones: add 218-699-7251.

Waterfront: not waterfront kept. ReserveMN gives Bear Paw sites 59E-70E (and 60, 61E) a lake distance of 150 ft (~46 m) and every other site .1 to .5 mile; imagery shows those sites behind a band of trees and a wide marsh/emergent-vegetation fringe on the Lake Itasca east arm, not open ground - at most a filtered view, no open frontage. Not a lakefront or lakeview upgrade.
Policy row: nothing contradicts it (check-in/check-out 4 p.m. and the one-vehicle/six-person site rule are park-level). Deer hunts Nov 7-15 and Nov 28-Dec 13, 2026 exclude the campgrounds.

Note cleaned: dropped '~100+ sites, electric available', 'showers and dump station', 'Reservable online' (fields hold them), and 'lakeside Bear Paw' (sites are ~150 ft back behind trees/marsh). 'horse/group camp' corrected: the DNR lists Elk Lake Group Camp and Lake Ozawindib Group Center, no horse camp.
Website OK (redirects to the new DNR park page).
